clue.text: Urge refusal to recognize item out of context

parts.note: to urge someone is to press them
cutting someone means pointedly ignoring them, a refusal to acknowledge them

explanation.surface: Someone urged to ignore a passage quoted out of its setting.
explanation.definitionFit: A clipping snipped from a newspaper is an article taken away from its surrounding pages.

clue.text: What a lot of cars still !

definitions.text: What a lot of cars still !

parts.words: What a lot of cars still !
parts.note: an exclamation about vehicles left stationary in a lot, i.e. a car park

explanation.surface: An exclamation at how many vehicles remain on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaving a vehicle stationary in a designated lot is what this activity means.

clue.text: Inspect what was once a pit

parts.note: ex means former, describing what something once was
a mine is a pit dug for coal or ore

explanation.surface: Surveying a disused colliery.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrutinise something closely is to look it over carefully.

clue.text: Tumbling over, she'll get a duck

indicators.note: tumbling shows the letters falling over and landing in a new order

explanation.surface: A woman who tumbles over will end up scoring nothing at cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a duck' looks like a cricket score of nought or a stumble; it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a dabbling duck with a broad spade-like bill.

clue.text: Mountains seen in natural setting

indicators.note: seen in signals that the letters lie concealed within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Peaks viewed in their wild surroundings.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the range dividing European Russia from Asia.

clue.text: The curses of old Greek citizens

parts.note: a ban is an old word for a curse or anathema

explanation.surface: The maledictions of the ancient Greeks.
explanation.definitionFit: These were people of Thebes, a leading city-state of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Unable right out to produce this universal theory

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are disordered and need rearranging

explanation.surface: A scientist fails to come up with a theory of everything.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective refers to the hypothesis that the solar system formed from a cloud of gas and dust in space.

clue.text: Small creatures that adhere to separate groups ?

parts.note: to stick in is to adhere or stay fixed in place
sects are breakaway religious or political groups

explanation.surface: Tiny animals that cling on to splinter factions.
explanation.definitionFit: These are twig-like insects, phasmids, camouflaged as twigs.

clue.text: " Rent-a-party " causes a storm

parts.note: rent as a past participle means ripped, i.e. torn
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A hired-in gathering of guests causes a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent-a-party' looks like hiring a crowd, but 'Rent' is the past tense of rend.
explanation.definitionFit: A twister is a violent rotating storm of wind.

clue.text: Gear for distilling drink with doctor in charge

parts.note: ale is a drink, a kind of beer
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A medic in charge of the drinks needs equipment to make spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old glass still used by alchemists to purify liquids.

clue.text: Old radio tuners are the tops

definitions.meaning: the fine wire contact used to tune early crystal radio sets
an idiom for the very best

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the thin wire on an early crystal wireless and also, idiomatically, something excellent.

clue.text: For whom, without Latin, cooking is foreign

parts.note: cui is the Latin for 'for whom' (as in cui bono)
sine is the Latin for 'without' (as in sine qua non)

explanation.surface: Someone for whom, lacking a classical education, fine food is foreign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Latin' tells you both pieces are Latin words; 'is foreign' hints that the answer is a French word.
explanation.definitionFit: This French borrowing means a style of cookery or food preparation.

clue.text: Badly rattles rising young actress

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters are put together wrongly and need rearranging

explanation.surface: A promising young performer is visibly shaken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' seems to belong to the wordplay, but it is part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A young actress tipped for fame is a little star of the screen.

clue.text: Pickwick's rascally companion loses head at fire

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter of the name is dropped

parts.note: Alfred Jingle is the roguish strolling player in Dickens's The Pickwick Papers

explanation.surface: A Dickens character's scoundrel friend is beheaded beside the hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingle is an old word for a fireplace or hearth fire, as in inglenook.

clue.text: It's a bit too much to bear, one gleans

definitions.text: It's a bit too much to bear, one gleans

parts.words: It's a bit too much to bear, one gleans
parts.note: the final small addition that makes something unbearable, read also as the final stalk a gleaner picks from a harvested field

explanation.surface: A gleaner, gathering the leftovers, finds it all a bit much to put up with.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from the final straw that breaks the camel's back, a burden's final tipping point.

clue.text: Not that Alonso really suffered it under thirty feet of water

definitions.text: Not that Alonso really suffered it under thirty feet of water

parts.words: Not that Alonso really suffered it under thirty feet of water
parts.note: in The Tempest Ariel sings that the drowned father lies full fathom five (thirty feet) and suffers a transformation, though Alonso is actually alive

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean king did not truly undergo a transformation at the bottom of the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Ariel's song 'Full fathom five thy father lies' tells Ferdinand his father Alonso has drowned and changed; five fathoms is thirty feet, and Alonso in fact survived.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase from Shakespeare now means any profound transformation.

clue.text: For health centres a rota is an anomaly

indicators.note: an anomaly is something irregular, so the letters are put out of their normal order

explanation.surface: A duty roster at health clinics turns out to be irregular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is an' belongs in the fodder, leaving 'anomaly' alone as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: These are hospitals for convalescents or long-term patients, the Latin plural form.

clue.text: Eminent but incompetent

definitions.meaning: read as '...', unable to do something

explanation.definitionFit: As one word it means distinguished; split in two it means lacking the ability.

clue.text: A roast for, champions?

definitions.meaning: a cut of beef from the hindquarter used for roasting
the ... is the team at the head of the league

explanation.definitionFit: It names a lean joint of beef and, split in two, the leading team.

clue.text: Drive a composer mad !

indicators.note: mad shows the letters going wild and being rearranged

explanation.surface: Something that would drive a musician crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Verdi was the Italian composer of Aida and La Traviata.

clue.text: Flier bloody-minded after grave .dereliction ?

parts.note: a winged creature thirsting for blood after deserting its tomb, the undead of folklore or the bat named after it

explanation.surface: An awkward pilot after a serious failure of duty.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the blood-drinking undead creature of legend, and also a bat that feeds on blood.

clue.text: They've just got engaged at the castle, that is the point

parts.note: the rook is the chess piece also called a castle
ie, id est, means that is
S, south, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A newly betrothed couple celebrate at a castle, which is the point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engaged' suggests betrothal but means taken on as new recruits.
explanation.definitionFit: Raw recruits are newcomers who have only just been taken on.

clue.text: Small blow from a tool

definitions.meaning: a light breeze that ruffles the surface of water
a person used by another as a dupe or instrument

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a faint ripple of wind on calm water and a stooge used to do someone's dirty work.

clue.text: Crop that has ears for the birds

definitions.text: Crop that has ears for the birds

parts.words: Crop that has ears for the birds
parts.note: a cereal plant whose grain grows in ears, fed to poultry; ears hint at hearing

explanation.surface: A harvest that listens to birdsong.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a cereal crop whose grain grows in ears and is used as chicken feed.

clue.text: Hesitate to speak where there's a Watergate plant

parts.note: to hem is to hesitate in speaking, as in hem and haw
a lock is literally a gate controlling water on a canal or river

explanation.surface: Someone hesitating to discuss the political scandal of the Nixon era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watergate' looks like the Nixon scandal, but it is read literally as a gate for water.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a poisonous umbelliferous herb, famously the poison that killed Socrates.

clue.text: All this was the Mikado's object

definitions.text: All this was the Mikado's object

parts.words: All this was the Mikado's object
parts.note: recalls the Mikado's song in Gilbert and Sullivan: 'My object all ...', the missing word describing the object

explanation.surface: A quotation about the aim of the emperor in a comic opera.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mikado sings 'My object all sublime I shall achieve in time', so the word fills that gap.

clue.text: Subtle ironies having greater effect on audience

indicators.note: subtle suggests the letters are artfully reworked into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Delicate irony lands better with listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subtle ironies' reads as a noun phrase, but 'Subtle' signals the anagram; the definition plays on loud sound reaching an audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Louder sounds make more impact on listeners' ears, a comparative adjective.

clue.text: Unshrinkable for all that

definitions.meaning: read as '...', i.e. never getting smaller
an idiom meaning however or despite this

explanation.definitionFit: Split into three words it describes something that never gets smaller; as one word it means in spite of that.
